subjects.meaningMnemonic: A tall box with a bar across the middle, like a window glowing with light. Picture the sun shining through it, so bright the glass seems split in two.
One flat line lying on its side. It is a single wooden plank laid across a muddy path so you can walk over it.
Three planks stacked and joined by one upright post, like the frame of a throne. Only a monarch gets to sit on something that sturdy.
A big empty square with nothing inside yet. It is a corral, a fenced pen waiting for animals to be herded in.
A tiny slanted dot, barely there. It is a speck of dust that landed on your page.
Two strokes leaning on each other like a pair of legs mid stride. This is a walker, always heading somewhere on foot.
One curved stroke sweeping down to the left. Hear the swoosh of a brush flicking across paper.
Two crossbars hung on a single post. Laundry gets draped over each bar, so this is a drying rack.
A bent little shape with a hand held out, hunched over and hoping. It is a beggar asking for spare change.
A figure with arms flung wide and legs spread apart. It looks just like a starfish lying flat on the sand.
One line across and one line down, crossing in the middle. It is a plus sign, the same one you use in maths.
Two flat lines, one above the other, the top one shorter. They are bunk beds, a small bunk stacked over a big one.
A trunk standing straight with branches above and roots spreading below. Someone shouts timber as it starts to fall.
A single straight line standing upright. It is a pole planted firmly in the ground.
A small square opening. It is a hatch in a ship's deck that you can pop open and climb through.
Many lines stream down from the top and flow out at the bottom. It is a head of long hair blowing in the wind.
Three points rise from one base, the middle one tallest. It is a ridge with three peaks against the sky.
A shape open at the top with walls on both sides. It is a bucket waiting to be filled.
A hand with a dot marking a spot on the wrist, the old way to measure a tiny length. That small measure is an inch.
A short line over a long line with a sprout pushing up between them. The long line is the ground, and the sprout grows out of rich soil.
Two halves facing each other with gaps between, like streets meeting from four sides. It is a crossroads in the middle of town.
This is only the left half of the crossroads, a narrow lane branching off. Call it a side street.
A big eye perched on top of two legs. It is a watcher who walks around and stares at everything.
A tall box with two bars inside, like an eye turned on its side. Picture a round eyeball rolling inside it.
Two long legs and nothing else, one bending out at the bottom. Someone is wobbling along on stilts.
A tall shape with a curved side and two bars inside. It is a thin crescent hanging in the night sky.
A slanted shape that seems to trail behind itself. It is someone walking slowly on dragging feet, in no hurry at all.
Two little loops twisted together. It is a tiny thread curled up after being pulled from a sweater.
A sharp blade on one side, ready to cut grain. It is a sickle swinging through a field.
Two short strokes point up and outward at the top. They are a pair of antlers poking out above a head.
Lines branch up from the soil like small leaves reaching for light. It is a seedling just breaking through.
A shape with an open frame like a raised palm. Slap it for a high five.
Two matching panels side by side with a gap between. They are saloon doors that swing open when you push through.
A straight stick with a short mark sticking off one side. It is a fortune stick shaken from a cup to tell your future.
A square split into four smaller squares. It is a paddy seen from above, divided into flooded plots.
The sun rises in the morning and sets at night. Everything that happens while the sun is up fills one whole day.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Each day you find a sunny niche by the window to sit in. Niche sounds like にち, the reading of day. It can also be read じつ in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: There is only one plank across the stream, so only one person can cross at a time. One plank means one.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Standing on that one plank, you get an itch on your back and cannot reach it without falling. Itch sounds like いち.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A monarch stands inside a corral with a speck of gold on the crown. Everything inside that fence belongs to the monarch, and that land is a country.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The whole country has one royal cook who feeds every citizen. Cook sounds like こく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The walker is always on the move. Every walker you pass on the street is a person.
subjects.readingMnemonic: That person is carrying a bottle of gin home after a long day. Gin sounds like じん. In some words it is read にん instead.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, a beggar pulls a plank off the drying rack and carves one notch in it. He adds a notch every time winter comes around, counting each year.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A kind nun gives the beggar a warm meal once a year. Nun sounds like ねん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: This starfish stretches its arms as wide as it can to look impressive. It wants you to see how large it is.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The large starfish took a bath in purple dye and now it glows. Dye sounds like だい. It can also be read たい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Write a plus sign and count its four arms, then count the ends and the middle twice for good luck. Somehow you always end up at ten.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You win ten shiny prizes, and every one is a jewel. Jewel sounds like じゅう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Bunk beds hold exactly two sleepers, one on top and one below. Bunk beds mean two.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Climbing to the top of the bunk beds, you bang your knee on the rail. Knee sounds like に.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Shout timber, and the tree falls onto a plank laid on the ground. The wood is pressed into paper and bound into a book.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A goose sees you reading that book and gives a loud honk. Honk sounds like ほん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A pole is pushed straight through the middle of a hatch. The pole is now in the hatch, right inside it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Stuck in the middle of the hatch, you chew on a sandwich while you wait. Chew sounds like ちゅう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Her long hair has not been cut in years and now reaches the floor. That hair is long.
subjects.readingMnemonic: She has to tie up all that long hair before she sits down to chow. Chow sounds like ちょう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A pole stands in a bucket at the foot of three peaks. Climb the pole, step over the peaks, and you exit the valley.
subjects.readingMnemonic: On your way to the exit, green shoots spring up wherever you step. Shoots sounds like しゅつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Put a plank under the bunk beds and you have three flat lines stacked up. Plank plus bunk beds makes three.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Three buckets of sand are piled on top of each other. Sand sounds like さん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: You push a stick an inch into the soil and watch its shadow move with the sun. The shadow tells you the time.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It is time to leave, so you jump into your jeep. Jeep sounds like じ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: At the crossroads you can turn down any side street you like. Whichever way you choose, you keep going.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Before going out, you grab your coat from the hook. Coat sounds like こう. It is also read ぎょう in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The watcher has one giant eyeball and walks around on stilts to get a better view. All it does is see.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The watcher sees a dog sleeping in its kennel. Kennel sounds like けん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A thin crescent hangs in the sky and slowly grows full, then shrinks again. That cycle takes one month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Once a month you try to get a good photo of the crescent. Get sounds like げつ. It is also read がつ for the months of the year.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Down a side street, someone walks on dragging feet, trailing a tiny thread from their coat. They are always lagging behind.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A goat trots behind them, nibbling the thread. Goat sounds like ご. It is also read こう in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A deer with antlers stands on a plank, holding a sickle under the crescent. It wants to go first and steps in front.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The deer calmly meditates before stepping in front, completely zen. Zen sounds like ぜん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A seedling pushes up through the ground and opens its first leaves. It is the start of a new life.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Every new life deserves a chance to say hello. Say sounds like せい. It is also read しょう in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A high five uses your whole hand. Count the fingers on that hand and you get five.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Five goats line up to give you a high five with their hooves. Goat sounds like ご.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The sun peeks through the gap between the saloon doors. That gap is an interval, the space between two things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Someone has wedged a can in the space between the doors to keep them open. Can sounds like かん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A fortune stick stands upright on a plank, pointing to the sky. It always points above.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A joker climbs up above everyone and juggles on the plank. Joker sounds like じょう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A pole of timber stands in the middle of the paddy, laid across with a plank. The sun rises right behind it every morning, because it faces east.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Facing east at dawn, you dip one toe into the cold paddy. Toe sounds like とう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Someone on stilts is trapped in a corral and pokes a stilt out of each corner. That makes four.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Four sheep wander into the corral to keep them company. Sheep sounds like し. It is also read よん and よ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: On its own, the kanji for day also means the sun itself, the thing that makes the day.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi ひ. Picture the sun so hot you shout "hee!" when it touches your skin.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The kanji for one plus the little つ ending is how you count one thing.
subjects.readingMnemonic: This uses the kun'yomi ひと plus つ. The つ ending is the native Japanese way of counting objects.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One plus day gives one day, or a whole day from morning to night.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use their on'yomi: いち from one and にち from day, which you already know.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is just the number one.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi いち, the same itch you remember from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a country or a region.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi くに, not the cook reading. Picture the royal cook saying "coo, nee" as he looks over his country.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One plus person means one person, or being all alone.
subjects.readingMnemonic: This is an irregular reading: ひとり. Learn it as a whole word; it does not use いち or じん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a person, someone.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi ひと, the same ひと you saw in 一人.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One person, then one person again: each person, one by one.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It is simply ひとり said twice: ひとりひとり.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a year, or a person's age in years.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi とし, not the nun reading. Picture the nun counting years on her toes, "toe, she" says.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A large person is a grown up, an adult.
subjects.readingMnemonic: This is an irregular reading, おとな. It does not use だい or じん; learn it as one word.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The kanji for large plus the い ending makes the adjective big.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi おお plus きい, so おおきい. Picture someone shouting "oh!" at something big.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Another way to say big, used right before a noun.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Same おお as 大きい, but it ends in きな instead of きい: おおきな.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Large turned into an adverb: very much, greatly.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi おお plus いに: おおいに.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Large in importance: something considerable or great.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Here the kanji uses its other on'yomi たい, plus した: たいした.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means large or great, often as a size label.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi だい, the purple dye from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Ten plus day gives ten days, or the tenth day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: This is a special date reading: とおか. Ten is read とお here and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number ten.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi じゅう, the jewel from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Two plus the つ counting ending: two things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi ふた plus つ: ふたつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Two plus person: two people, a pair.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Like 一人, this is irregular: ふたり. Learn it together with ひとり.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Two plus day: two days, or the second day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: ふつか. It does not use に or にち.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number two.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi に, the knee from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Twenty plus day: twenty days, or the twentieth day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special reading: はつか. Learn it as one word, because none of the usual readings appear.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Two tens make twenty; this word means twenty years old.
subjects.readingMnemonic: When it means twenty years old, it has its own reading: はたち. A big birthday gets a special word.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a book.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi ほん, the honk from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The book's own person: the person in question, the one themselves.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: ほん plus にん, the second reading of person.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The sun's origin: the land where the sun rises, Japan.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Day becomes に and book stays ほん: にほん. The stronger form にっぽん doubles the sound.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the inside of something.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi なか. Picture the inside of a box so dark you say "nah, ka" and back away.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Inside, then inside again: quite deeply, so very or considerably.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It is なか said twice: なかなか. The 々 mark repeats the kanji before it.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Inside the year: all year round.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi, with a sound change: ねん plus じゅう, so ねんじゅう. The ちゅう of inside picks up a voiced sound.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Inside the day: during the daytime.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: にち plus ちゅう, squeezed into にっちゅう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The kanji for long plus the い ending: the adjective long.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi なが plus い: ながい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Exit as a verb: to leave or to go out.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi で plus る: でる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To make something exit: to take it out or put it out.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi だ plus す: だす. Compare でる, where you go out yourself.

meanings.text: to go out (e.g. on an excursion or outing)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To exit the house on an outing: to go out.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It starts with the kun'yomi で, then かける: でかける.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Three plus day: three days, or the third day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: みっか. Three is read みっ and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Three plus the つ counting ending: three things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi みっ plus つ: みっつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number three.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi さん, the sand from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Time, then time again: from time to time, sometimes.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It is とき said twice, and the second one softens to どき: ときどき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One plus hour: one o'clock, or one moment in time.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: いち plus じ, the jeep from the kanji: いちじ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means time or a moment.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi とき, not the jeep reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Going as a verb: to go.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi い plus く: いく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Going about a task: to perform or carry it out.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the longer kun'yomi おこな plus う: おこなう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The going part of a trip: the way there.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi い plus き: いき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: See as a verb: to see or to watch.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi み plus る: みる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To make someone see: to show.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi み plus せる: みせる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To see something you were looking for: to find it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi み plus つける: みつける.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To be seeable: to be visible or in sight.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi み plus える: みえる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To get seen at last: to be found.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi み plus つかる: みつかる. Compare みつける, where you do the finding.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One plus month: a span of one month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi ひと plus つき: ひとつき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the Moon, or a month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi つき, not the get reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Years and months together: a long stretch of time.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kun'yomi: とし plus つき: としつき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Behind as a place: the back or the rear.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi うし plus ろ: うしろ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means after, or what comes behind.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi あと, not the goat reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the front, or before.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi まえ, not the zen reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Life arriving: to be born.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi う plus まれる: うまれる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Life as a verb: to live.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi い plus きる: いきる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To bring something to life: to produce or cause it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the on'yomi しょう plus じる: しょうじる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means life or living.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi せい, the say from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One life: a whole lifetime.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi, squeezed: いち plus しょう becomes いっしょう.

meanings.text: born in (country, month, imperial era, zodiac year, etc.)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Your birth, or the place you were born.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi う plus まれ: うまれ, like 生まれる without the る.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A person's life.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: じん plus せい, the gin and the say: じんせい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Five plus the つ counting ending: five things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi いつ plus つ: いつつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number five.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi ご, the goat from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Five plus day: five days, or the fifth day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: いつか. Five is read いつ and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The interval of time: time, an hour, a period.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: じ plus かん, the jeep and the can: じかん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the space between things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi あいだ, not the can reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The one between people: a human being.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: にん plus けん, and けん softens to げん: にんげん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The span of a year: during a year.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: ねん plus かん, the nun and the can: ねんかん.

meanings.text: to move something (to a higher place)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To move something above: to raise it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi あ plus げる: あげる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means above or on top.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi うえ, not the joker reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To go above: to rise or go up.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Here it uses the kun'yomi あ plus がる, so あがる, like あげる but going up by itself.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means east.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi ひがし, not the toe reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Four plus day: four days, or the fourth day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: よっか. Four is read よっ and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Four plus the つ counting ending: four things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi よっ plus つ: よっつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number four.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi し, the sheep from the kanji. People also say よん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Two strokes spread down and out from one point at the top, like the cloth of an open umbrella. Hold this umbrella over whatever sits beneath it.
A pointed top over stacked bars, with a glint on each side at the bottom. It is a heavy ingot, freshly cast and ready for the vault.
Two short strokes part and sweep outward, one to the left and one to the right. Together they look like a mustache under a big nose.
A short stroke crosses a long one that bends sharply and kicks out at the end. That sharp bend is an elbow, cocked and ready to nudge someone.
Two strokes lean together to make a low, pointed opening. It is the mouth of a tunnel you have to duck to get into.
A round little head, arms stretched out to the sides, and one leg curled under. It is a toddler wobbling across the floor.
Three short strokes rise and fan out at the top of a shape. They are wisps of steam drifting up from something hot.
A flat top with both edges hanging down at the sides. It is a blanket thrown over something to keep it covered.
Boxes stacked one on another under a pointed roof, with a wide frame at the base. It is a tower rising high over the town.
A small dot pressed down onto a flat line. It is a thumbtack pinning a note to the top of a board.
Two upright posts joined by a bar across the top, open at the bottom. It is a goalpost waiting for someone to score.
A slanted moon with a stroke cutting through it, half hidden by cloud. The sun has gone down and it is dusk.
A cross with little sparks shooting off in four directions. It is a sparkler fizzing in your hand at a summer festival.
Thin lines drift sideways and curl down at the end. It is your breath, floating out into the air on a cold morning.
One drop falls straight down and two droplets jump out to either side. It is a little splash in a puddle.
One stroke folds back on itself and curls out at the bottom, like a long graceful neck. It is a swan gliding across a pond.
A short slanted stroke and a long one that bends into a scoop at the bottom. It is a ladle for serving soup.
Lines of words pile up on top of an open mouth. It is a megaphone, making every word loud enough to hear across the field.
A long stick with a crossbar pokes out of an open mouth. Someone is happily sucking on a lollipop.
A figure with crossed legs and one arm swung wide, caught in the middle of a spin. It is a dancer twirling on the stage.
A tall post with short rungs sticking out on one side. It is a ladder leaning on the wall, waiting to be climbed.
A tall box with a little slanted spout on top. It is a milk carton, full of something white.
A hand grips a long upright stick crossed by several lines. It is a quill held ready to write.
Rain starts pouring, so you snap open your umbrella over a plank bench and sit right there. You need shelter now, not later.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Under the umbrella you eat an ice cream cone right now, before it melts. Cone sounds like こん. On its own it is read いま.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Under an umbrella, a monarch with a huge mustache and a crown of antlers counts a pile of ingots. Every single one is made of gold.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Only the king may touch that gold. King sounds like きん. It is also read かね when it means money.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Your bent elbow sticks out just like the curl of the number nine. Before every game you bend it nine times, never more than nine.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Then you pick up your pool cue and line up the shot. Cue sounds like きゅう. It is also read く in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The tunnel has a low, pointed opening. Duck your head and enter.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Inside the tunnel, a little newt scurries in ahead of you. Newt sounds like にゅう. As a verb it is read はい or い.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A toddler hides under a blanket with a book, thinking so hard that steam rises from its head. Even this little one loves to study.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Grown ups gawk at the toddler who studies all night. Gawk sounds like がく. As a verb it is read まな.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A thumbtack holds a flag on the roof of a tower. Climb up through a hatch, past a goalpost on the balcony, and you see just how tall it is.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It is so tall and windy at the top that you need a coat. Coat sounds like こう. On its own it is read たか.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A ball sails through the goalpost, bounces off a pole, and spins around a plank pinned down with a thumbtack. It keeps rolling in a perfect circle.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It rolls round and round with no end. End sounds like えん. The same word is the yen, the money of Japan.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A toddler waves its arms and wobbles across the room. Every toddler is a child.
subjects.readingMnemonic: At bedtime the child counts sheep to fall asleep. Sheep sounds like し. On its own it is read こ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: At dusk you take your fortune stick and go read it under the open sky. You cannot read a fortune indoors; you have to be outside.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Outside, a guy is already waiting with his own fortune stick. Guy sounds like がい. On its own it is read そと.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: This mustache has four curls on each side. Count them all and you get eight.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Trimming all those curls takes a tiny hatchet and a steady hand. Hatchet sounds like はち. It is also read や in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A thumbtack pins a fake mustache to the wall. It has exactly six hairs, so this one means six.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Six rocks hold the mustache down when the wind blows. Rock sounds like ろく. It is also read む in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A plank lies flat with a pole hanging down from it, and a fortune stick dangles off the end of the pole. Everything here points down, below the plank.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You park your car below the bridge to keep it out of the rain. Car sounds like か. It is also read げ, and した on its own.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: You fix a pole between the bunk beds with a thumbtack, light a sparkler, and stand it on a log of timber. It is the signal for your friends to come over.
subjects.readingMnemonic: They come carrying loaves of rye bread. Rye sounds like らい. As a verb it is read く, as in くる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A beggar lets out a long breath on a cold day. A speck of light swirls through it with a swoosh, and you can feel his spirit.
subjects.readingMnemonic: That spirit is the key to his good mood. Key sounds like き. It is also read け in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One drop falls and makes a splash, with two droplets jumping out to the sides. It is only a little splash.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The little splash puts on a show for the ants nearby. Show sounds like しょう. On its own it is read ちい, as in ちいさい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A swan grips a ladle in its beak and stirs the pond with a swoosh. It always stops after exactly seven stirs.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Then it dries the ladle on seven clean sheets. Sheet sounds like しち. It is also read なな.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Three peaks rise from one wide base against the sky. Put them together and you have a mountain.
subjects.readingMnemonic: At the foot of the mountain the ground turns to soft sand. Sand sounds like さん. It is also read せん, and やま on its own.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Someone pops out of a hatch with a lollipop in one hand and a megaphone in the other. They will not stop telling you a long tale.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The tale is all about a giant waffle. Waffle sounds like わ. As a verb it is read はな, as in はなす.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The dancer spins across the stage in a long gown. She is a woman who owns the spotlight.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Every morning the woman goes for a jog before practice. Jog sounds like じょ. On its own it is read おんな.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Climb the ladder with a ladle in your hand and point it at the stars. The handle points to the North Star, so you know which way is north.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Up north, everyone plays ice hockey. Hockey sounds like ほく. On its own it is read きた.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, a beggar hangs his only shirt on a drying rack shaped like a plus sign. He waits for the sun to climb to the top of the sky, because by noon it will be dry.
subjects.readingMnemonic: At noon every day a goat wanders over to nibble the shirt. Goat sounds like ご.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Line up milk cartons along a long plank. Keep going until the plank holds one hundred of them.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A thirsty yak drinks all one hundred cartons. Yak sounds like ひゃく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: You sit in the sun with a quill and a blank page. Dip the quill in ink and start to write.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You write a story about the sea shore. Shore sounds like しょ. As a verb it is read か, as in かく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, someone leaps off the soil onto a pair of stilts and strides away. Up there they are always ahead, there before everyone else.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Being ahead, they spot a lucky cent on the path before anyone. Cent sounds like せん. On its own it is read さき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: At dusk it is too dark to see faces, so you open a hatch and call out. Everyone answers with their name.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A lion shakes its mane when it hears its name. Mane sounds like めい. On its own it is read な.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Now plus day: this day, today.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special reading: きょう. Learn it as one word; the formal こんにち uses both on'yomi, as in こんにちは.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Now plus year: this year.
subjects.readingMnemonic: An irregular reading: ことし. It uses neither こん nor ねん, so learn it as a whole word.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means now, the present moment.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi いま, not the cone reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Now plus month: this month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: こん, the cone from now, plus げつ, the get from month: こんげつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Now with にも on the end: at any moment, right on the verge of happening.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi いま plus にも: いまにも.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Now plus after (the kanji for behind): everything after now, from now on.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: こん, the cone, plus ご, the goat from behind: こんご.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Now with に added: before long, any time now.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi いま plus に: いまに.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Gold with the polite お in front: money.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi かね after the polite お: おかね.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji can mean money, or metal in general.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi かね, not the king reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number nine.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi きゅう, the cue from the kanji. You will also hear く.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Nine plus day: nine days, or the ninth day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: ここのか. Nine is read ここの and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Nine plus the つ counting ending: nine things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi ここの plus つ: ここのつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To make something enter: to put it in, or to let someone in.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi い plus れる: いれる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Enter as a verb: to go in or come in.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi はい plus る: はいる. Compare いれる, where you put something else in.

meanings.text: former imperial university of Japan (established under the ritsuryō system for the training of government administrators)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Large plus study: the large place of study, a university.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: だい, the dye, plus がく, the gawk: だいがく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Study plus life: someone whose life is study, a student.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: がく, the gawk, plus せい, the say from life: がくせい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Enter plus study: entering a school, admission.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: にゅう, the newt, plus がく, the gawk: にゅうがく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: University plus life: a university student.
subjects.readingMnemonic: All three on'yomi: だい plus がく plus せい: だいがくせい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Middle (the kanji for in) plus study: the middle stage of school, junior high school.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: ちゅう, the chew, plus がく, the gawk: ちゅうがく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Study as a verb: to learn.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi まな plus ぶ: まなぶ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means learning or scholarship.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi がく, the gawk from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Tall plus the い ending: the adjective tall or high. A high price is expensive, so it means that too.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi たか plus い: たかい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Circle plus the い ending: the adjective round.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi まる plus い: まるい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a circle, and also the yen, the money of Japan.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi えん, the end from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a child or a kid.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi こ, not the sheep reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Outside plus country: a country outside your own, a foreign country.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: がい, the guy, plus こく, the cook: がいこく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Foreign country plus person: a person from a foreign country, a foreigner.
subjects.readingMnemonic: All three on'yomi: がい plus こく plus じん, the gin from person: がいこくじん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the outside, out in the open air.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi そと, not the guy reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Outside plus exit: you exit to the outside, so it means going out.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: がい, the guy, plus しゅつ, the shoots from exit: がいしゅつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To put something outside its place: to remove it, take it off, or undo it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi はず plus す: はずす.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Eight plus the つ counting ending: eight things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi やっ plus つ: やっつ. The shorter やつ also appears.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Eight plus day: eight days, or the eighth day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: ようか. Eight is read よう and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number eight.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi はち, the hatchet from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Six plus the つ counting ending: six things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi むっ plus つ: むっつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Six plus day: six days, or the sixth day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: むいか. Six is read むい and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number six.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi ろく, the rock from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means below, the space down under something.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi した, not the car reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Below as a verb: to go down, or to come down from somewhere high.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi お plus りる: おりる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To make something go below: to lower it, or to let it hang down.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi さ plus げる: さげる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Below as a verb: to come down, to go down, to fall.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi さ plus がる: さがる. It is usually spelled 下がる, while 下る on its own is often read くだる.

meanings.text: train heading toward the ending point of its route

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Going below: the way down, such as a downhill slope or a train heading out to the end of its line.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi くだ plus り: くだり.

meanings.text: to lower (a hand, flag, shutter, etc.)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To bring something below: to take it down, or to lower it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi お plus ろす: おろす. It is usually spelled 下ろす, while 下す on its own is often read くだす.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Something handed down to you from above: someone kindly gives it to you.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi くだ plus さる: くださる. It is the polite verb behind ください.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Come plus year: the year that is coming, next year.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: らい, the rye, plus ねん, the nun from year: らいねん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: さ in front of next year pushes it one further: the year after next.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It is さ plus らいねん: さらいねん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Come plus month: the month that is coming, next month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: らい, the rye, plus げつ, the get from month: らいげつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Come as a verb: to come, or to arrive.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi く plus る: くる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: さ in front of next month pushes it one further: the month after next.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It is さ plus らいげつ: さらいげつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Exit plus come makes できる, to be able to. Add だけ and it means as much as you can.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Exit is read で and come is read き: できる, then だけ: できるだけ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means next or coming, as in next year or next spring.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi らい, the rye from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means spirit, mind, or the feeling in your heart.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi き, the key from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Large plus spirit (air): the great body of air around the earth, the atmosphere.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Large uses its other on'yomi たい, plus き, the key: たいき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Something enters your spirit and suits it well: you like it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Spirit is read き, then に, then enter is the kun'yomi い plus る: きにいる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Person plus spirit: the warm feeling people have for something, popularity.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Person uses its second on'yomi にん, plus き, the key: にんき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Little plus さい: the adjective small or little.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi ちい plus さい: ちいさい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Like 小さい, but it sits right before a noun: a small something.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi ちい plus さな: ちいさな.

meanings.text: short month (i.e. having fewer than 31 days)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji marks something small, such as a small size or a short month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi しょう, the show from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Seven plus day: seven days, or the seventh day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: なのか. Seven is read なの and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number seven.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi しち, the sheet from the kanji. You will hear なな just as often.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Seven plus the つ counting ending: seven things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi なな plus つ: ななつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a mountain or a hill.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi やま, not the sand reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Tale as a verb: to talk, or to speak.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi はな plus す: はなす.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a talk, a chat, or a story someone tells.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi はなし, not the waffle reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Woman plus の plus child: a female child, a girl.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kun'yomi: おんな, then の, then こ: おんなのこ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a woman.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi おんな, not the jog reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Woman plus child: a girl, or women as a group, as on a girls' team.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: じょ, the jog, plus し, the sheep from child: じょし.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the north.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi きた, not the hockey reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Noon plus behind: the part of the day behind noon, the afternoon.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: ご, the goat from noon, plus ご, the goat from behind: ごご.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Noon plus in front: the part of the day in front of noon, the morning.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: ご, the goat, plus ぜん, the zen from in front: ごぜん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number one hundred.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi ひゃく, the yak from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Write as a verb: to write something down.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi か plus く: かく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the point or tip, the part that goes before the rest.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi さき, not the cent reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Before plus life: someone whose life started before yours and who now guides you, a teacher.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: せん, the cent, plus せい, the say from life: せんせい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Before plus month: the month before this one, last month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: せん, the cent, plus げつ, the get from month: せんげつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Before everything else: first of all, to begin with.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the rare kun'yomi ま plus ず: まず. You will often see it written in kana.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Before plus day: a day before today, the other day.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: せん, the cent, plus じつ, the second on'yomi of day: せんじつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Name plus in front: the name you put in front of yourself, your name.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kun'yomi: な plus まえ: なまえ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a name or a title.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi な, not the mane reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Name plus person: a person who has made a name for themselves, a master or expert.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: めい, the mane, plus じん, the gin from person: めいじん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Three lines run down side by side, the middle one a little shorter. Water trickles along between them like a creek.
A tall jet shoots up the middle with water spraying out to both sides. It is a fountain in the town square.
A bent stroke with a hook, like an arm curled up tight. Flex it and show off your muscle.
A square jar with a lid on top and two lines poking up inside. It is a cookie jar, and somebody keeps sneaking a hand in.
A wide roof of cloud with four drops falling inside it. It is a steady drizzle that soaks everything.
Two blades cross in the middle with two little handles poking up on top. It is a pair of scissors, open and ready to snip.
A tall frame with ridges inside and one side stretching down low. It is an earlobe, the soft bit you can tug.
A lid on top, a box of food underneath, and a little spoon at the side. It is your lunchbox, packed and ready.
A box on an axle with a wheel at each end, seen from above. It is a wagon rolling down the road.
A slim figure standing tall at the left edge of a kanji, always beside someone else. It is a sidekick, never the hero but always there.
A straight line drops down and curls back up at the bottom. It is a fishhook dangling on its line.
A rounded frame with two little eggs tucked inside. It is a bird nest, warm and well guarded.
A frame with one long bar slashing straight through it. It is a barricade that says nobody gets past.
A figure in the middle with sparks leaping off both sides. It is a campfire crackling in the dark.
Like soil, but here the top line is the long one, standing proud over a short base. It is a knight with chest out, ready to serve.
A stroke folds over and crosses itself, like two fingers twisted together. Keep your crossed fingers up and hope for luck.
Each line here is a little creek trickling down the hill. Three creeks running side by side join up into one strong stream.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Toss a cent into the stream and make a wish. Cent sounds like せん. On its own it is read かわ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh of the pen, you draw a plus sign, then another, and another. You keep going until you have drawn a thousand.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Each one earns you a cent, so a thousand of them make ten dollars. Cent sounds like せん. It is also read ち in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The fountain in the town square sprays out in every direction. What pours out of every fountain is water.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The fountain water tastes surprisingly sweet. Sweet sounds like すい. On its own it is read みず.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A deer with antlers stands between the bunk beds, and a pole runs down the middle like a giant plus sign. It splits the room exactly in half.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Give me your hand and I will give you half my snack. Hand sounds like はん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A farmer puts every muscle into plowing the rice paddy. In the old picture, this strong worker in the field stands for a man, a male.
subjects.readingMnemonic: When the plowing is done, he does a little victory dance. Dance sounds like だん. It is also read なん, and おとこ on its own.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Every evening you leave the cookie jar on the windowsill where the sun goes down. The jar always faces the setting sun, toward the west.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Say goodbye to the sun as it sinks in the west. Say sounds like せい. It is also read さい, and にし on its own.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A drizzle falls over the rice paddy, and a swan stretches its neck up into the storm. Lightning strikes, and the whole paddy crackles with electricity.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You hide in your den until the power comes back on. Den sounds like でん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: With scissors you trim a block of timber into a desk and pin a notice to it with a thumbtack. You are at school, and the notice says it is time for your exam.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You left your coat at school on the day of the exam. Coat sounds like こう. It is also read きょう in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Someone climbs out of a hatch, gives you a high five, and shouts into a megaphone. Every word comes out loud and clear.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Even the goat learns a few words. Goat sounds like ご. As a verb it is read かた, as in かたる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Kneel in the garden and pat the soil flat with both hands. This kanji is simply soil, the earth that everything grows in.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Mix the soil with water and it turns into a lump of dough. Dough sounds like ど. On its own it is read つち.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Long before anyone shouts timber, the trunk stands tall with branches above and roots below. It is a living tree.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You pick a bouquet of blossoms from the tree. Bouquet sounds like ぼく. It is also read もく, and き on its own.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: You press your earlobe right up against the saloon doors. You cannot see inside, but you can hear.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Through the doors you hear someone order a sticky bun. Bun sounds like ぶん. It is also read もん, and き as a verb, as in きく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: You open your lunchbox at noon and find it packed to the lid. There is only one thing to do with it: eat.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You get a shock when a frog jumps out of your lunchbox. Shock sounds like しょく. As a verb it is read た, as in たべる, or く, as in くう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Bolt an engine onto the wagon and it no longer needs a horse to pull it. Now it is a car.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A shark sits behind the wheel, honking at everyone. Shark sounds like しゃ. On its own it is read くるま.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Your sidekick lies on a plank, dangling a fishhook through a hatch in the floor. Something big tugs on the line, and you both gasp: what?
subjects.readingMnemonic: Whatever it is, it pulls so hard that a whole car comes up through the hatch. Car sounds like か. On its own it is read なに, or なん before some sounds.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A deer with antlers sets up a drying rack under a goalpost and paints a plus sign on top. The laundry dries fast because it faces the warm sun, which means it faces south.
subjects.readingMnemonic: In the south they bake warm naan in clay ovens. Naan sounds like なん. On its own it is read みなみ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, a pole spins across a plank, again and again. It spins ten thousand times before it stops.
subjects.readingMnemonic: One patient man counts every spin. Man sounds like まん. It is also read ばん in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A beggar builds a barricade around a bird nest to guard the eggs. He checks on it again and again, every single day.
subjects.readingMnemonic: He has to, because hungry mice keep sneaking past the barricade. Mice sounds like まい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Tip the milk carton and pour. What comes out is white.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A hawk swoops down to sip the white milk. Hawk sounds like はく. On its own it is read しろ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A starfish climbs to the top of the bunk beds, then onto a plank laid across them, reaching up and up. It is trying to touch the heavens.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It pitches a tent up in the heavens. Tent sounds like てん. It is also read あま in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Behind the barricade sits a bird nest, and one bird never leaves it. She keeps the eggs warm because she is their mother.
subjects.readingMnemonic: When the eggs hatch, the mother takes her chicks out on a boat. Boat sounds like ぼ. On its own it is read はは.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Sparks leap up from the campfire into the night sky. Every campfire starts with one thing: fire.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Never park your car too close to the fire. Car sounds like か. On its own it is read ひ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, a plank slides across a hatch. You always push it shut with your right hand.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Green ooze leaks out of the right side of the hatch. Ooze sounds like う. It is also read ゆう, and みぎ on its own.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A knight wobbles up on stilts with a blanket over his shoulders and a megaphone in his hand. He unrolls a long scroll and begins to read.
subjects.readingMnemonic: He reads the news aloud to every ship down at the dock. Dock sounds like どく. As a verb it is read よ, as in よむ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, you throw a plank across the stream and walk over it side by side, crossed fingers held up for luck. The one who crosses with you is your friend.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Your friend is a unicorn who always lets you ride on its back. Unicorn sounds like ゆう. On its own it is read とも.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a river or a stream.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi かわ, not the cent reading. After a place name it often softens to がわ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number one thousand.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi せん, the cent from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means water, especially cool water.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi みず, not the sweet reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means half, or partly.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi はん, the hand from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Half plus ば: the halfway point, the middle of something.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi なか plus ば: なかば.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Large plus half: the larger half, more than half, the majority.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Large uses its other on'yomi たい, plus はん, the hand: たいはん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Male plus の plus child: a male child, a boy.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kun'yomi: おとこ, then の, then こ: おとこのこ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a man.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi おとこ, not the dance reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Male plus の plus person: a male person, a man.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kun'yomi: おとこ, then の, then ひと: おとこのひと.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Male plus child: a boy, or men as a group, as on a boys' team.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: だん, the dance, plus し, the sheep from child: だんし.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the west.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi にし, not the say reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Electricity plus spirit: the power in the wires, and the electric light it gives.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: でん, the den, plus き, the key: でんき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Electricity plus talk: talk carried by electricity, a telephone call.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: でん, the den, plus わ, the waffle from tale: でんわ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Electricity plus child: the tiny child of electricity, an electron, and so electronic.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: でん, the den, plus し, the sheep from child: でんし.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Study plus school: a place for study, a school.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi, squeezed together: がく becomes がっ before こう, the coat: がっこう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Middle plus school: the middle school, junior high school.
subjects.readingMnemonic: ちゅう, the chew, plus がっこう, the school word you already know: ちゅうがっこう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: School plus chief (the kanji for long also means leader): the head of a school, the principal.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: こう, the coat, plus ちょう, the chow from long: こうちょう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Little plus school: the school for little ones, elementary school.
subjects.readingMnemonic: しょう, the show, plus がっこう: しょうがっこう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: High school plus life: someone living the high school life, a high school student.
subjects.readingMnemonic: こうこう, the word for high school, plus せい, the say from life: こうこうせい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Tall plus school: the high school, senior high school.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi, and both are こう, two coats in a row: こうこう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Word plus study: the study of words and languages.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: ご, the goat, plus がく, the gawk: ごがく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a word or a language.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi ご, the goat from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Word as a verb: to tell, or to talk about something at length.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi かた plus る: かたる.

meanings.text: Japanese language (esp. as a school subject in Japan)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Country plus language: a country's own language, such as the Japanese class at school.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: こく, the cook, plus ご, the goat: こくご.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means earth, soil, or dirt.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi つち, not the dough reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a tree or a bush.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi き, not the bouquet reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Hear as a verb: to hear, to listen, or to ask.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi き plus く: きく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Hear with こえる on the end: a sound reaches your ears, so it can be heard.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi き plus こえる: きこえる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Eat as a verb: to eat.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi た plus べる: たべる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A rougher way to say eat: to eat, or to make a living.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi く plus う: くう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Electricity plus car: a car that runs on electricity, an electric train.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: でん, the den, plus しゃ, the shark: でんしゃ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a car, or any vehicle.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi くるま, not the shark reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means what, or how many.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi なん here, and なに in other places, not the car reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: What plus か: some what, so something or anything.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi なに plus か: なにか. In casual speech it shrinks to なんか.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: What plus で: by what, so why or how.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi なん plus で: なんで.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: What plus でも: whatever it is, so anything at all.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi なん plus でも: なんでも.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: What plus とか: something or other, or getting by somehow.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi なん plus とか: なんとか.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the south.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi みなみ, not the naan reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number ten thousand, or a huge number of things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi まん, the man from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Ten thousand plus one: a one in ten thousand chance, the unlikely worst case.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: まん, the man, plus いち, the itch from one: まんいち.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Every plus day: every day, daily.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: まい, the mice, plus にち, the niche from day: まいにち.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Every plus year: every year, yearly.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: まい, the mice, plus ねん, the nun: まいねん. People also say まいとし, with the kun'yomi of year.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Every plus month: every month, monthly.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: まい, the mice, plus げつ, the get: まいげつ. You will also hear まいつき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the color white, and from that, innocence.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi しろ, not the hawk reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: White plus the い ending: the adjective white, or blank like an empty page.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi しろ plus い: しろい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Heavens plus spirit: the mood of the sky, the weather.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: てん, the tent, plus き, the key: てんき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Mother with the polite お in front and さん after it: mom.
subjects.readingMnemonic: An irregular reading: mother is read かあ here, so おかあさん. Learn it as a whole word.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means fire or a flame.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi ひ, not the car reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the right side, or your right hand.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi みぎ, not the ooze reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Read as a verb: to read, or to recite aloud.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi よ plus む: よむ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Read plus write: reading what others have written, the reading of books.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: どく, the dock, plus しょ, the shore from write: どくしょ.

meanings.text: reading (of a kanji, esp. kun reading)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Read as a noun: a reading, such as the reading of a kanji.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi よ plus み: よみ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a friend or a companion.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi とも, not the unicorn reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Friend plus person: a person who is your friend.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: ゆう, the unicorn, plus じん, the gin from person: ゆうじん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A flat top, a flat bottom, and one post between them. It is a steel girder, the beam builders bolt into every frame.
A small bent stroke with a tail, pointed like a tiny triangle. It is a stone arrowhead you might dig up in a field.
Three short teeth sticking out from one side of a bar. Drag this rake across the lawn and it gathers the leaves.
A frame with a little tick on top and lines inside like a face. It is a self portrait an artist painted while staring in a mirror.
A small stand with a mark on top, like a table with an offering on it. People bow in front of this altar.
Two sets of marks splaying out left and right at the top. They are footprints in the snow, heading off in two directions.
Soil on top and a long slanting stroke cutting through it. That slant is a walking cane, leaning on the ground for support.
A curling stroke that loops and snaps back on itself. It is a whip, cracking through the air.
Two horns on top and a body made of stacked lines. It is a ram, lowering its curled horns to charge.
A post with many crossbars and two legs that dig into the dirt. It is an old wooden plow pulled across a field.
A dot on top, a crossbar, and an arm pointing off to the side. It is a signpost showing travelers which way to go.
A blade on top and a long handle swinging down. It is a woodcutter axe, ready to split a log.
A tall shape that narrows to a sharp point at the bottom. It is a chili pepper, so hot it makes your eyes water.
A dot on top, a little stand, and a long base on the ground. It is a podium where a speaker steps up to talk.
A bent pole with streaks hanging down from it. It is a banner flapping in the wind at a parade.
An eyeball shape sitting on two small legs. It is a clam peeking out of its shell on the beach.
Two prongs joined by a crossbar, like the handles of a tool. They are pliers, gripping something tight.
A curved top and lines branching from a center stroke like fingers. It is an open palm, raised to wave hello.
A stroke with a hook at the bottom and a dot at the top right. It is a tent stake hammered into the ground.
A paddy sitting on top of soil. Fields on good land make a farmstead, where a family lives and farms.
A swoosh of wind knocks a plank off the girder, and it always falls to the left side.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You hold the saw in your left hand. Saw sounds like さ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Your sidekick leans against a big timber and closes their eyes. After all that work, it is time to rest.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Your coach gives you the cue to sit down and rest. Cue sounds like きゅう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The scissors on their own stand for father, who always cuts the birthday cake into fair slices.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Father cooks a pot of food for the whole family every Sunday. Food sounds like ふ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A drizzle falls from the sky, then grows heavier until it becomes real rain.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Rain soaks the ground until mud starts to ooze between your toes. Ooze sounds like う.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: People climb down from bunk beds, grab an umbrella, and follow the arrowhead sign to a big meeting.
subjects.readingMnemonic: At the meeting everyone flies a kite in the park. Kite sounds like かい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A goalpost stands around a hatch with a plank across it. Every goalpost on the field looks exactly the same.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Two deer in the forest look the same, so you cannot tell which doe is which. Doe sounds like どう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A plank, a hatch, a fishhook, and a rake are piled in the shed. Sorting them out is a matter you keep putting off.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You park the jeep by the shed while you deal with the matter. Jeep sounds like じ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The self portrait shows one big eyeball staring back. It is a picture of oneself.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You paint yourself driving a jeep. Jeep sounds like じ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Soil is piled around an altar in the middle of the office, because the company prays for good sales.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The company logo is a smiling shark. Shark sounds like しゃ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Footprints lead out from under bunk beds and run off on stilts. Someone made a quick departure.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Everyone tosses their hats in the air at the departure. Hats sounds like はつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A person with a walking cane shuffles along in the sun. Someone is out for a walk.
subjects.readingMnemonic: That someone is a shark with a cane. Shark sounds like しゃ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A whip cracks against the soil and leaves a mark in the ground.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A cheetah races across the ground. Cheetah sounds like ち.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A monarch with antlers rides a ram pulling a plow across timber, a pole, and a plank. Running all that is a big business.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The business sells nothing but gyoza. Gyoza sounds like ぎょう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The signpost on its own shows a direction to go.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A farmer points a hoe in the right direction. Hoe sounds like ほう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A woodcutter axe chops timber, a chili pepper, and antlers, and a thumbtack pins them to a podium. It is a brand new art piece.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You bang your shin on the new piece. Shin sounds like しん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A banner flies over soil in the sun, with a plank to sit on. That is the place to be.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A joker juggles in the middle of the place. Joker sounds like じょう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A mustache, an eyeball, a hatch, and a clam all wear name tags. Each one is an employee.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Every employee lives at the same inn. Inn sounds like いん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The podium on its own means to stand up. Step onto it and stand tall.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You stand up in a field of tall ritzy reeds. Ritzy sounds like りつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Saloon doors swing open. A swoosh of pliers pulls a plank off the bunk beds blocking the way.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You open the door and kites fly in. Kite sounds like かい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The palm on its own is a hand, held open.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You put a shoe on your hand like a puppet. Shoe sounds like しゅ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Muscle on its own means power. Flex a muscle and you feel its strength.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A rook in a chess game has the power to sweep across the whole board. Rook sounds like りょく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A hatch sits behind saloon doors. Every cowboy who walks in stops to ask a question about what is behind it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A curious monk keeps asking the same question all day. Monk sounds like もん.

meanings.text: counter for decades of ages, eras, etc.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Your sidekick pulls up a tent stake and puts a new one in its place. That stake is a substitute.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The substitute stake is painted with bright dye. Dye sounds like だい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The sun and the crescent shine side by side, so the sky is never dark. Everything looks bright.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A horse shakes its mane in the bright sunlight. Mane sounds like めい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A pole, a plank, and the sun sit on a farmstead. A muscle with a swoosh of effort makes them all move.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A doe moves quickly through the field. Doe sounds like どう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The left kanji on its own: the left side.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi ひだり.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Left and right, side to side.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: さ from left and ゆう from right.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Rest plus the み ending makes a noun: a rest or a break.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi やす plus み. A rest from work is a day you take to yourself.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The verb form of rest: to rest or take a day off.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi やす plus む. You rest your body by not going to work.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Father with polite words on both sides: dad.
subjects.readingMnemonic: 父 is read とう here, an irregular reading, with the polite お and さん around it.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The rain kanji on its own means rain.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi あめ. Picture rain falling so hard you shout "ah, meh!"

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Meeting as a verb: to meet someone.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi あ plus う.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A meeting of tales: a conversation.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: かい from meeting and わ from tale.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Coming out and meeting: an encounter.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi で from exit and あ from meeting, plus い.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The country's meeting: the National Diet.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses こっ, a shortened こく from country, and かい from meeting.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A large meeting: a convention or tournament.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: たい from large and かい from meeting.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A meeting or assembly.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the on'yomi かい, the kite hook.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Come out and meet: to run into someone.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi で from exit and あ from meeting, plus う.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Same plus the じ ending means same or identical.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi おな plus じ. Two things that look the same are おなじ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Same and one: one and the same, identical.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: どう from same and いつ from one. It is one and the same thing.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Same plus time means the same time.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: どう from same and じ from time.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A large matter: something important.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: だい from large and じ from matter.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The matter of eating: a meal.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: しょく from eat and じ from matter.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A fire matter: a fire that burns a building.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: か from fire and じ from matter.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The matter kanji on its own: a thing or matter.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi こと.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Something that came out: an event.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi で and き, then ごと, a voiced こと (rendaku).

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A matter worth seeing: splendid.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi み from see and ごと, a voiced こと (rendaku).

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A meeting company: a corporation.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: かい from meeting and しゃ from company.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Companies meeting together: society.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: しゃ from company and かい from meeting.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The long, senior person of a company: the president.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: しゃ from company and ちょう from long.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Exit and depart: a departure.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses しゅっ from exit and ぱつ, はつ with a p sound after the small っ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Setting out and seeing: a discovery.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses はっ from departure and けん from see.

meanings.text: publication (of a newspaper, magazine, book, etc.)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Sending it going: publication.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses はっ from departure and こう from going.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The car departs: a train or bus leaving.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses はっ from departure and しゃ from car.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The one in front: the former.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: ぜん from in front and しゃ from someone.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Someone who studies: a scholar.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: がく from study and しゃ from someone.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Someone on their own: a person.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi もの, sometimes said もん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The one behind: the latter.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: こう from behind and しゃ from someone.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The ground kanji on its own: earth or ground.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the on'yomi ち, the cheetah hook.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Below the ground: underground.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: ち from ground and か from below.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The raw ground of clothing: fabric.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the irregular き from life and じ from ground.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Soil and ground: a plot of land.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: と from soil and ち from ground.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A direction, or a polite word for a person.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi かた.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One direction: one side, or on the other hand.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses いっ from one and ぽう, ほう with a p sound after the small っ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Many persons: people, politely.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi かた, then がた, voiced (rendaku). The 々 repeats the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A direction of the land: a region.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: ち from ground and ほう from direction.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: New things you hear: a newspaper.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use on'yomi: しん from new and ぶん from hear.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: New as an adjective.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Little loops twist down to a base with three tails. It is a spool, its thread winding round and round.
Two dots lean on a long handle crossed by a bar. It is a measuring scoop, with grains spilling off the side.
One stroke zigzags down and then runs long and flat along the bottom. It is a slide in the playground.
A roof with two little legs under it, an opening in the ground. It is a burrow where a rabbit hides.
A bent stroke with a sharp edge hooking down. It is a cleaver hanging in the kitchen.
A slanted cliff with a small square box at its foot. That box is a pebble that rolled down.
A box on top of a shape that kicks out to the side. It is a sneaker, ready to run.
Two short drops, one over the other, hanging on the left. They are icicles dripping from the eaves.
Soil on top and a leg stretching long underneath. It is a sprinter pushing off the ground.
A stroke that bends back on itself and curls up at the end. It is a coil of rope on a dock.
A wagon under a blanket rides the conveyor belt. The belt will carry it all the way to town.
